main.title: IBM 701
main.summary: Announced on May 21, 1952, the IBM 701 was IBM's first commercial scientific computer.

cards.heading: IBM 701
cards.text:
The IBM 701 Electronic Data Processing Machine, known as the Defense Calculator while in development, was IBM's first commercial scientific computer and its first series production mainframe computer, which was announced to the public on May 21, 1952. It was designed and developed by Jerrier Haddad and Nathaniel Rochester and was based on the IAS machine at Princeton.

The IBM 701 was the first computer in the IBM 700/7000 series, which were IBM's high-end computers until the arrival of the IBM System/360 in 1964.

The business-oriented sibling of the 701 was the IBM 702 and a lower-cost general-purpose sibling was the IBM 650, which gained fame as the first mass-produced computer.

main.title: The DNA double-helix model is published
main.summary: James Watson and Francis Crick published their double-helix model of DNA in 1953, drawing crucially on X-ray evidence from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.

cards.heading: The DNA double-helix model is published
cards.text: James Watson and Francis Crick published their double-helix model of DNA in 1953, drawing crucially on X-ray evidence from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins. The model described two chains coiled around each other, joined through paired bases: adenine with thymine, and cytosine with guanine. Each chain has a sugar-phosphate backbone carrying those bases in sequence. This structure helped explain the molecule that carries genetic instructions for growth, development, functioning and reproduction. A complex biological role could now be studied through a specific molecular arrangement.

main.title: NTSC colour television
main.summary: The United States adopted an NTSC colour television standard in 1953 that worked with existing black-and-white sets.

cards.heading: NTSC colour television
cards.text: The United States adopted an NTSC colour television standard in 1953 that worked with existing black-and-white sets. Colour broadcasts could therefore reach new receivers while older televisions continued to display the picture in monochrome. It built on the American analogue standard adopted in 1941 and became one of the three major colour systems alongside PAL and SECAM. The NTSC name later served as shorthand for related digital video formats, commonly associated with 480 active lines and frame rates of 30 or 29.97 frames per second.

main.title: Brown v. Board of Education
main.summary: In 1954, the US Supreme Court ruled that state-enforced racial segregation in public schools violated the Fourteenth Amendment.

cards.heading: Brown v. Board of Education
cards.text: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, 347 U.S. 483 (1954), is a landmark decision of the United States Supreme Court that ruled that U.S. state laws establishing racial segregation in public schools violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment, even if the segregated facilities are equal in quality. The decision partially overruled the Court's infamous 1896 decision Plessy v. Ferguson, which had ruled that racial segregation laws were constitutional as long as the facilities for each race were equal, a doctrine that had come to be known as "separate but equal". The Court's unanimous decision in Brown and its related cases paved the way for integration and was a major victory of the civil rights movement, and it became a model for many future impact litigation cases.

main.title: Godzilla
main.summary: Godzilla is a 1954 Japanese epic kaiju film directed and co-written by Ishirō Honda, with special effects by Eiji Tsuburaya.

cards.heading: Godzilla
cards.text:
Godzilla is a 1954 Japanese epic kaiju film directed and co-written by Ishirō Honda, with special effects by Eiji Tsuburaya. Produced and distributed by Toho, it is the first film in the Godzilla franchise. The film stars Akira Takarada, Momoko Kōchi, Akihiko Hirata, Takashi Shimura, with Haruo Nakajima and Katsumi Tezuka as Godzilla. In the film, Japanese authorities deal with the sudden appearance of a gigantic monster, mutated from nuclear bomb testing. 

Godzilla entered production after a Japanese-Indonesian co-production collapsed. Tsuburaya originally proposed a giant octopus before the filmmakers decided on a dinosaur-inspired creature. Godzilla pioneered a form of special effects called suitmation in which a stunt performer wearing a suit interacts with miniature sets. Principal photography ran 51 days, and special effects photography ran 71 days.

main.title: Seven Samurai
main.summary: Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai appeared in 1954, following villagers who hire warriors to defend their harvest from bandits.

cards.heading: Seven Samurai
cards.text: Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai appeared in 1954, following villagers who hire warriors to defend their harvest from bandits. Kurosawa wrote the film with Shinobu Hashimoto and Hideo Oguni after research uncovered an account of samurai protecting peasants. The writers spent more than six weeks developing the script and detailed character plans. Toho's production involved studio work and location filming in Shizuoka and Kanagawa, with costs exhausting the budget midway through. The completed story of collective defence became an influential work of world cinema.

main.title: Bell Labs presents its silicon solar cell
main.summary: Bell Labs developed a practical silicon solar cell in 1954, converting light directly into electricity through the photovoltaic effect.

cards.heading: Bell Labs presents its silicon solar cell
cards.text: Bell Labs developed a practical silicon solar cell in 1954, converting light directly into electricity through the photovoltaic effect. Individual cells could be combined into modules, the building blocks of solar panels. Their electrical behaviour changes when light reaches them, allowing a solid-state device to supply power without mechanical movement. Silicon became the dominant material in commercial photovoltaic production, alongside a smaller range of thin-film technologies. The Bell Labs development helped establish a practical foundation for the solar panels that would follow.

main.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
main.summary: The Fellowship of the Ring was published in Britain on 29 July 1954 as the first volume of The Lord of the Rings.

cards.heading: The Fellowship of the Ring
cards.text: The Fellowship of the Ring was published in Britain on 29 July 1954 as the first volume of The Lord of the Rings. Tolkien's Middle-earth narrative alternates threatening journeys with the shelter of welcoming houses, giving danger and comfort distinct rhythms. Concerning Hobbits introduces the setting before the main narrative, itself divided into two books. The Shadow of the Past and The Council of Elrond became particularly discussed chapters. The Two Towers and The Return of the King would continue the larger work begun in this volume.

main.title: Disneyland
main.summary: Disneyland is a theme park at the Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, California, United States.

cards.heading: Disneyland
cards.text:
Disneyland is a theme park at the Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, California, United States. It was the first theme park opened by the Walt Disney Company and the only one designed and constructed under the direct supervision of Walt Disney, opening on July 17, 1955.

Disney initially envisioned building a tourist attraction adjacent to his studios in Burbank to entertain fans who wished to visit; however, he soon realized that the proposed site was too small for the ideas that he had. After hiring the Stanford Research Institute to perform a feasibility study determining an appropriate site for his project, Disney bought a 160-acre (65 ha) site near Anaheim in 1953. The park was designed by a creative team hand-picked by Walt from internal and outside talent. They founded WED Enterprises, the precursor to today's Walt Disney Imagineering. Construction began in 1954 and the park was dedicated during a special televised press event on the ABC Television Network on July 17, 1955, a day before its public opening.

main.title: Montgomery bus boycott
main.summary: The Montgomery bus boycott was a political and social protest campaign against the policy of racial segregation on the public transit system of Montgomery, Alabama.

cards.heading: Montgomery bus boycott
cards.text: The Montgomery bus boycott was a political and social protest campaign against the policy of racial segregation on the public transit system of Montgomery, Alabama. It was a foundational event in the civil rights movement in the United States. The campaign lasted from December 5, 1955 – the Monday after Rosa Parks, an African-American woman, was arrested for her refusal to surrender her seat to a white person – to December 20, 1956, when the federal ruling Browder v. Gayle, a United States Supreme Court decision that declared the Alabama and Montgomery laws that segregated buses were unconstitutional, took effect.
